entries.name: Wyrrabalong National Park

Northern section: drive north on Wilfred Barrett Drive; southern section: via The Entrance Road then Bateau Bay Road. No entry fee is stated on the visitor-info page.
Wikivoyage: the park preserves one of the last few remaining coastal rainforests of the Central Coast.

entries.name: Great North Road

facts.claim: The Old Great North Road - World Heritage walk is a 9 km loop (3.5-4.5 hours, grade 4) in Dharug National Park along a convict-built road overlooking the Hawkesbury, past a quarry with convict graffiti, stone buttresses, culverts and a curved wall; there is a Convict Road app.
The road was built by up to 720 convicts between 1826 and 1836; Dharug National Park is always open but may close for weather or fire danger.
The Great North Road is on the Australian National Heritage List and the UNESCO World Heritage list as part of the Australian Convict Sites.

entries.name: Wisemans Ferry

Wikivoyage: a small town established by an ex-convict in 1817, about an hour from Sydney, with colonial architecture, parks and river picnics; Wisemans Ferry Park has a beach, barbecues, playgrounds and a cafe by the ferry entrance.
NPWS: Dharug National Park is reached from Wisemans Ferry, by car ferry or on foot.

entries.bio: A Hawkesbury River village with a free 24-hour cable ferry, in use since 1829, and the gateway to Dharug National Park.

entries.name: Yengo National Park

facts.claim: Yengo National Park is part of the Greater Blue Mountains Area World Heritage Property, a rugged landscape of gorges and ridges for 4WD, car, mountain bike or foot, with Aboriginal sacred sites and rock engravings, and the convict-built Old Great North Road in the south-east.

Finchley lookout looks across remote wilderness to Mount Yengo, with Aboriginal rock engravings at nearby Finchley campground; 4WD is required in wet weather, there is no public transport, and the Big Yango precinct is behind locked gates needing a permit.
The park is always open but may close for weather or fire danger.
Mount Yengo (Big Yengo) is 668 m high; the park covers 154,328 ha, about 91 km southwest of Newcastle.
